rationale: All three lenses ran cleanly against the supplied plan.md spec. 6 real findings survive triage: four unconfirmed-reachability gaps in the new _normalized_model_name regexp_replace chain (no case-insensitive matching, and incomplete coverage for multi-segment region prefixes, nested routing prefixes, and extended version-suffix shapes — kept major per this task's own established precedent of not dismissing unconfirmed-but-plausible variants), a missing test asserting actual row-level cost/session/token aggregation after the GROUP BY key change (existing tests only pin SQL shape and a pure-Python regex mirror), and one commit in the MR range not following the ticket-prefixed commit-message format. The acceptance lens also flagged 3 spec-text deviations (invoke/ prefix stripped beyond the plan's literal 'exactly three things', a date-stamp-anchored suffix strip narrower than the plan's literal pattern, and an ORDER BY expression instead of an alias) — all three are deliberate, already fixed and human-approved in this task's own prior review round (visible in the diff's own embedded code-review-check.json/decisions.jsonl, including a live-DB-verified approval), so they are not re-raised as new blocking findings, though plan.md's Global Constraints/Review Focus text is now stale and should be updated to match the shipped, already-approved behavior. 7 items dismissed as noise, by-design scope limits, or already-resolved; 0 deferred.

findings.title: Normalization assumes lowercase routing/region/provider tokens
findings.problem: None of the three chained regexp_replace calls pass the 'i' (case-insensitive) flag, so a routing prefix, region token, or provider segment arriving in any case other than lowercase (e.g. 'Converse/US.Anthropic.claude-...') will not match any of the three patterns.
findings.impact: A mixed-case model_name variant is left completely unnormalized and fragments into its own breakdown row instead of merging with the canonical lowercase variant; no test exercises a mixed-case input.
findings.recommendation: Add the 'i' flag to all three regexp_replace calls, or confirm and test that upstream ingestion guarantees lowercase for these tokens.

findings.title: Routing-prefix strip anchored to string start only
findings.problem: '^(converse|invoke)/' only matches when the routing token is literally the first thing in the string; a routing prefix nested behind another wrapper segment (e.g. 'bedrock/converse/us.anthropic...') never matches because of the '^' anchor.
findings.impact: Such a variant is left entirely unnormalized, including the region/provider part that would otherwise be reachable, so it continues to fragment the breakdown report. Reachability in current production CLI telemetry could not be confirmed from this review.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether any nested-prefix form is reachable in production data; if so, loosen the anchor or strip the outer wrapper first.

findings.title: Region-prefix strip doesn't handle multi-segment prefixes
findings.problem: '^([a-z0-9-]+\.)?anthropic\.' matches at most one leading dot-segment before 'anthropic.'; a compound prefix with two or more dot-segments (e.g. 'aws.us-east-1.anthropic.') leaves the outer segment(s) unstripped.
findings.impact: Such a variant retains a residual prefix and continues to fragment the breakdown report instead of merging into the canonical row. Reachability in current production data could not be confirmed from this review.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the optional group ('(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)*anthropic\.') so any number of leading dot-segments are stripped, or confirm at most one region segment can ever precede 'anthropic.' in production data.

findings.title: Version-suffix strip is end-anchored and brittle to trailing extras
findings.problem: '(\d{8})-v\d+:\d+$' requires the inference-profile tag to be the literal end of the string; a variant with extra trailing characters or segments after the version tag (e.g. '-20251001-v1:0:1' or '...-v1:0-prod') does not match.
findings.impact: That variant keeps its full suffix and does not collapse with the bare-date canonical form, re-fragmenting the breakdown for that model. Reachability of such suffix shapes in production Bedrock data could not be confirmed from this review.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether extended suffix shapes occur in production; if so, loosen the trailing anchor or add an explicit case for them.

findings.title: Missing test for numeric aggregation across merged variants
findings.problem: All new tests assert either the generated SQL string shape or a pure-Python mirror of the regex chain; none exercises get_model_breakdown against sample cost_daily rows carrying two raw-name variants of the same model and asserts the merged row's session_count/cost_usd/total_tokens.
findings.impact: The actual behavior this fix exists to deliver — correct aggregation after the GROUP BY key changes — has no regression test; a future change could reintroduce incorrect summation (e.g. double-counting sessions across variants) without failing any test.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that feeds get_model_breakdown two raw-name variants of one model within the same window/session and asserts the single merged output row's session_count/cost_usd/total_tokens are correctly summed and deduped.

findings.title: Commit message doesn't follow ticket-prefixed format
findings.problem: Commit 8a76e9b8c ('normalize-model-name-regional-prefixes: add planning artifacts') in this MR's range does not use the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format.
findings.impact: Violates the repo's documented commit-message convention (.ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md), which every other commit in this same MR correctly follows.
findings.recommendation: Reword via rebase/squash to 'EPMCDME-15523: Add planning artifacts', or squash all commits into one ticket-prefixed commit per the guide's default squash-merge strategy before merging.
